WITH order_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    ordersmark,
    AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain
  FROM orderexecutions
  WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY ordersmark
),
first_bench_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS first_benchmark
  FROM order_avg
),
above_first AS (
  SELECT 
    oa.ordersmark,
    oa.avg_remain,
    (oa.avg_remain - fb.first_benchmark) AS excess_first
  FROM order_avg oa
  CROSS JOIN first_bench_calc fb
  WHERE oa.avg_remain > fb.first_benchmark
),
second_bench_calc AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS second_benchmark
  FROM above_first
),
above_second AS (
  SELECT 
    af.ordersmark,
    af.avg_remain,
    af.excess_first,
    (af.avg_remain - sb.second_benchmark) AS excess_second
  FROM above_first af
  CROSS JOIN second_bench_calc sb
  WHERE af.avg_remain > sb.second_benchmark
)
SELECT
  AVG(avg_remain) AS avg_of_remaining,
  AVG(excess_first) AS avg_excess_over_first,
  AVG(excess_second) AS avg_excess_over_second
FROM above_second;

assumptions.assumption: The dataset contains at least one order (ordersmark group, including NULLs as one group) whose average remaincount exceeds both the first and second benchmark thresholds. If this precondition is not met, the output columns will be NULL rather than numeric values.
